name: 2-pin speaker terminal (JST PH)
//: Where a speaker's two wires meet the board. A speaker is not a module, so nobody lists one, and an amplifier's two outputs then each end on a net with one member: the board does not route, and every amplifier ended "the chain is broken" (the council on PR #98, C-3). This is the other end of those nets — pick it beside the amplifier, as the power inlet is picked beside a motor driver. The speaker itself stays off the board, a drawer entry with no record.
//power: Both pins are INPUTS on the speaker rail, each naming the side of the pair it takes (`polarity`), so each joins the net its side of the amplifier drives: SPK+ on SPEAKER_P, SPK- on SPEAKER_N. There is no ground pin, on purpose: the output is bridged, and the speaker's return is the pair's other side.

power.note: To the speaker's + wire, from the amplifier's + output. Never to ground.
To the speaker's - wire, from the amplifier's - output. Never to ground: it swings, it is not a return.

pin_order_proof.source: Pad 1 is SPK+: this record's own convention for a 2-pin speaker terminal, as jst-ph-2-power-inlet's pad 1 is VCC — not read from a document. Mark SPK+ on the silkscreen, and wire the speaker's own + to it.

body_mm.source: The JST PH 2-pin housing B2B-PH-K-S as spark's jst-ph-2-power-inlet records it from JST's PH series drawing: 7.9 mm across, 5.8 mm deep with the latch — not read again for this record
body_mm.why_it_matters: Only where a generated layout leaves room for the plug; no connection depends on it.

contact_rating_a.source: JST PH series datasheet, current rating per contact, as jst-ph-2-power-inlet records it — not read again for this record
contact_rating_a.why_it_matters: The speaker's current passes through it: 3 W into 4 ohm is about 0.87 A RMS (the square root of 3/4), within it; a lower impedance or a larger amplifier moves that.

host_requirements: NEVER ground either pin. The amplifier's output is bridged: SPK+ and SPK- both swing and the speaker sits across them, so a pin that meets a ground, or another output, shorts the amplifier.

This connector and any other 2-pin JST PH on the board — the power inlet's above all — can be cross-plugged. Key one of them or use another series: a motor supply into an amplifier output destroys it.
The speaker's impedance decides the current through this terminal and what the amplifier delivers: check it against the amplifier's record before choosing a speaker.

simulation.skip: a terminal is wiring, not a part to simulate; the amplifier it hangs off has no Wokwi part either, and no sound reaches the simulation
